neighbours.label: the determiner slot where business prose sets up an employer noun next (worked for our [clients], been with the [company], for you and your [business]), as opposed to the same determiners where no employer noun is expected
fire: Most of our drivers have been with the company for over a decade.
Let us show you what we can do for you and your team.
Maria has worked for our firm since it first opened its doors.
Several engineers have stayed with our business through two recessions.
He has been with the company longer than anyone in the office.
Call today to learn how we can help you and your staff.
Our accountant has served our customers for nearly twenty years.
Few employees remain with one company for their whole career.
quiet: Most of the children have been with the teacher since the morning.
Let us know what you saw on the walk by the river.
Maria has lived near the river since she was a child.
Several hikers have stayed with the group through two storms.
He has been with the band on tour longer than anyone else.
Call today if you see the lost cat near the park.
Our cat has slept on the same chair for nearly ten years.
Few swallows remain in the barn after the first frost.

predictions: employment/service frames 0.3-0.6 on the determiner; frames with no employer expectation below 0.05
notes: Card: ' our' x6, ' your' x6, ' the' (been with the company), ' member' (its member companies), ' this' (what this company is about); - pole promotes ' company', ' business'. Probe: 'stayed with our firm' 0.608, 'been with the company' 0.385, 'worked for our clients' 0.309, 'you and your business' 0.296; but 'worked in our garden' 0.278 and 'you and your garden' 0.296 also fire (the frame, not the noun, carries it); 'hikers ... with the guide' 0.003, sentence-initial 'Our dog' 0.008.
